A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found that the most important factors for sustainability in SESs are the presence of social capital, the ability of users to make collective choices about their resources, and the presence of institutions that can resolve conflicts and enforce decisions.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the likelihood of achieving a sustainable SES is not a function of a single variable but rather a function of the interactions among all variables.
